subject: Private deploy ops readiness: network & account prerequisites
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-corp.com>, itops@acme-corp.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Private deploy ops readiness: network & account prerequisites

Hi Samir / Acme infra team,

Thanks again for agreeing to the private deployment walkthrough this week. To keep momentum we pulled together a concise ops readiness checklist so your infra and security teams can validate prerequisites ahead of the install window. Attached: "redwood_private_readiness_v1.xlsx" (spreadsheet) and a sample CIDR text file.

Top-line items we need from you before we start the installer run (please see attachment for detailed fields):

1) Network & IPing
- Primary public egress range (CIDR) for outbound TLS (so we can whitelist in your proxy).
- Private peering/CIDR plan for nodes (recommended: /16 for larger clusters; see worksheet).
- Desired MTU (we recommend 1500 unless jumbo frames are required).

2) Firewall & Ports (inbound rules to allow from Redwood jumpbox or VPC):
- 443/tcp (HTTPS) to control plane endpoints
- 22/tcp (SSH) to bastion only (no direct node SSH)
- 6443/tcp (Kubernetes API) restricted to control plane CIDRs
- 9090/tcp (Prometheus) and 3000/tcp (Grafana) if you want metrics forwarded to your monitoring
- 9091/tcp (agent metrics) - optional

3) Service accounts & auth
- A service account for the installer with ability to create service accounts / roles (we provide a JSON template in the sheet).
- KMS/HSM details if using customer-managed key encryption for secrets.

4) Registry & images
- URL for private container registry and credentials or a pull-through proxy.
- If images must be air-gapped, confirm transfer mechanism and checksum file.

5) Logging & auditing
- Destination for audit logs (S3/GCS/On-prem syslog) and retention policy.
- Any SIEM ingestion endpoints and contact for testing.

6) Time and name resolution
- NTP source(s) and DNS entries we should create (we will provide the required hostnames).

7) Contact matrix and escalation
- Primary and secondary contacts for netops, security, and platform (with cell numbers).

Action items for Redwood: we will provision a temporary jumpbox IP and provide an installer container with instructions. Please fill the attachment and confirm the CIDRs so we can generate the exact firewall rules.

If you prefer, we can run a 30-minute technical call to walk the checklist line-by-line.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Jonas, thanks — this checklist is exactly what NetOps needs. A few quick notes from our side: 

- Public egress: 34.120.0.0/18 (we will add a policy to allow outbound TLS to Redwood egress ranges once you confirm the specific destinations).
- Internal cluster CIDR: planning to use 10.20.0.0/16 for nodes, 10.21.0.0/24 for services.
- We use an internal Harbor registry at registry.acme-corp.local:8443. We will create a pull service account for redwood-installer and share creds in a secure envelope.
- MTU is 1500.
- KMS: We have a Vault HSM integration; will provide admin contact in the spreadsheet.

Questions: 
1) Do you require BGP peering or will static routes suffice for the initial deployment?
2) For audit logs, we prefer S3-compatible endpoint at s3.acme-corp.local with 365d retention. Are log batching settings configurable on your side?

NetOps will add the temporary jumpbox IP once you publish it and we will coordinate a firewall rule change for the installer window (Thu 09 Apr preferred).
